declarations.name: FadeCommand
declarations.comment:
A command type for color fading during immersive media playback.

You use a color fade to either fade into the video frame from a requested color, or fade out of the video frame to a requested color.
The fade commands are usually used for fading in at the start of the  playback and fading out at the end of the playback. These
commands are also used during immersive camera view switches during the playback.

Fade commands can be absolute time-based or offset-based. If absolute time-based, then `time` dictates
the time it needs to start executing and keep fading until the `duration` property value. On the other hand if they are offset based,
then the `offset` dictates the fade percentage from the start `time` of the fade command until the `duration` of the fade.
If the fade has to start at time `0.0` second of the playback for duration of `1.0` seconds and if the media FPS is `90`, then first frame is
accompanied with presentation metadata that has fade command with `0.011` as offset, the second frame has fade command
with offset of `0.022`, and so on; the 90th frame has an offset of `1.0`.

members.signature: init(id: Int, time: CMTime, duration: CMTime, direction: FadeCommand.FadeDirection, color: simd_float3, offset: CMTime? = nil)

Initializes a color fade command.
- Parameters:

  - duration: The duration of the command. This can be `.zero` if the command has no duration.
  - direction: The fade direction for this command instance.
  - color: The fade color.
  - offset: The offset from the start time of this command. This parameter is usually unused and let in control of a `PresentationDescriptorReader`.

declarations.name: FadeEnvironmentCommand
declarations.comment:
A command type for opacity fading environment backdrops during immersive media playback.

Use opacity fade to apply the requested opacity to the AIV environment backdrops. Fade environment commands can be absolute time-based or offset-based.
If fade environment commands are absolute time-based, `time` dictates the time it needs to start executing and keep fading until the `duration` property value.
If the fade environment commands are offset-based, then `offset` property dictates the fade percentage from the start `time` of the fade environment command until the `duration` of the fade.
For example, if the fade starts at `0.0` of the playback for a duration of `1.0` seconds and if the media FPS is 90, then first frame
is accompanied with presentation metadata with the fade environment command, which has an offset of `0.011`. The second frame has a fade
environment command with offset of `0.022` seconds, and so on, giving 90th frame an offset of `1.0`.

declarations.name: ImmersiveCamera
declarations.comment:
A type that holds all the information for an immersive media camera needed to process and render immersive media video frames.

This type holds information about camera identifier, camera type, default presentation rate, camera pose, and camera calibration data.
Immersive media content is captured using more than one camera calibrated lens. Hence it's necessary to use different geometry for each lens
to render the corresponding video clips. AIV content creators should be able to add or remove any camera at any point during
the creation and iteration process.

members.name: pose
members.comment:
The pose of this immersive camera.

The rotation component of the pose decomposes into three axis rotations, applied
intrinsically in this order:
1. **Roll** — rotation around the camera's local z-axis (the optical axis; the camera looks toward −Z).
2. **Yaw** — rotation around the camera's (post-roll) local y-axis.
3. **Pitch** — rotation around the camera's (post-roll, post-yaw) local x-axis (the right / baseline axis).

This matches Spatial's `EulerAngleOrder.xyz`, which composes intrinsically as roll, then
yaw, then pitch (equivalently, extrinsically as pitch, then yaw, then roll). The composition
order matters — the same angle values under a different order produce a different
orientation. In particular, this does **not** match `RealityKit.Transform(pitch:yaw:roll:)`,
which composes intrinsically as yaw, then pitch, then roll.

### Stereo fusion constraints

The rotation component is applied uniformly to both eyes as an image reorientation; it
does not remap eye assignment, reproject parallax, or account for the stereo baseline
encoded in the source video. For stereo (`stereoCamera`) content, only rotations that
keep the stereo baseline horizontal in viewer space produce comfortable fusion:

- **Roll** — rotates the baseline out of horizontal, creating vertical disparity between
  eyes. Small roll angles cause eye strain; larger angles (≥ a few degrees) prevent
  fusion entirely.
- **Yaw** — may be safe in some circumstances but increasingly likely to cause anomalous parallax perception at larger angles.
- **Pitch** — the baseline is the rotation axis and the invariant of the rotation depends on the projection.
- Any mixed rotation that decomposes to a non-zero roll component exhibits the same
  failure proportional to the roll magnitude.

For mono content there are no stereo constraints and the full rotation space is valid.

members.name: metadataItem
members.comment:
Builds a metadata item containing the presentation commands active at the start of
the specified frame's time range.

This is intended to be called once per video frame. The returned item's `time` and
`duration` are set directly from `frameTimeRange`, so the caller can write it into
a per-frame metadata track without further clipping or stamping. Returns `nil` if
no presentation commands are active at `frameTimeRange.start`.

- Parameter frameTimeRange: The frame's presentation time range. Its `start` is
  used to resolve which commands are active; the returned item is stamped with the
  full range.
- Returns: An `AVMetadataItem` whose value encodes the active presentation commands
  for that frame, or `nil` if none are active.

members.name: metadataTrack
members.comment:
Retrieves all metadata items to write to an output metadata track, optionally clipped
to a segment time range. Pass a `timeRange` to produce one item per segment (e.g. per
IDR group or per fixed-length interval).

Note: the last item's `duration` may be invalid, since the descriptor itself doesn't
know where the video ends. If you need a concrete duration (e.g. to extend the final
segment to the end of the video), copy the returned item and overwrite `duration` with
the valid value. Also, use the same timescale for `timeRange` as the
``PresentationCommand`` values to avoid timescale mismatches.

- Parameter timeRange: The segment range to filter to, or `nil` to return all items.
- Returns: An array of `AVMetadataItem` objects sorted by start time.

members.name: rotation
members.comment:
Camera rotation to override the rotation in ``ImmersiveCamera/pose``.

The rotation decomposes into three axis rotations, applied intrinsically in this order:
1. **Roll** — rotation around the camera's local z-axis (the optical axis; the camera looks toward −Z).
2. **Yaw** — rotation around the camera's (post-roll) local y-axis.
3. **Pitch** — rotation around the camera's (post-roll, post-yaw) local x-axis (the right / baseline axis).

This matches Spatial's `EulerAngleOrder.xyz`, which composes intrinsically as roll,
then yaw, then pitch (equivalently, extrinsically as pitch, then yaw, then roll). The
composition order matters — the same angle values under a different order produce a
different orientation. In particular, this does **not** match
`RealityKit.Transform(pitch:yaw:roll:)`, which composes intrinsically as yaw, then
pitch, then roll.

### Stereo fusion constraints

The rotation is applied uniformly to both eyes as an image reorientation; it does not
remap eye assignment, reproject parallax, or account for the stereo baseline encoded
in the source video. For stereo content, only rotations that keep the stereo baseline
horizontal in viewer space produce comfortable fusion:

- **Roll** — rotates the baseline out of horizontal, creating vertical disparity
  between eyes. Small roll angles cause eye strain; larger angles (≥ a few degrees)
  prevent fusion entirely.
- **Yaw** — may be safe in some circumstances but increasingly likely to cause anomalous parallax perception at larger angles.
- **Pitch** — the baseline is the rotation axis and the invariant of the rotation depends on the projection.
- Any mixed rotation that decomposes to a non-zero roll component exhibits the same
  failure proportional to the roll magnitude.

For mono content there are no stereo constraints and the full rotation space is valid.

declarations.name: VenueDescriptor
declarations.comment:
The Apple Immersive Media Venue Descriptor is a collection of static metadata necessary
for every Apple Immersive Video.

This type contains information that includes camera definitions such as the lens calibration information, as well as
data necessary for the rendering of the video frames.

members.name: unownedExecutor
members.signature: nonisolated final var unownedExecutor: UnownedSerialExecutor { get }
members.comment:
Retrieve the executor for this actor as an optimized, unowned
reference.

This property must always evaluate to the same executor for a
given actor instance, and holding on to the actor must keep the
executor alive.

This property will be implicitly accessed when work needs to be
scheduled onto this actor.  These accesses may be merged,
eliminated, and rearranged with other work, and they may even
be introduced when not strictly required.  Visible side effects
are therefore strongly discouraged within this property.

- SeeAlso: ``SerialExecutor``
- SeeAlso: ``TaskExecutor``
